# orca requirement

Every `orca requirement` command. Ids: a full id, a unique prefix, or (projects) a name or path.

## `orca requirement show <group>`

a requirement's rounds, drafts and document

- What it does: reads from the panel (no write).
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix

## `orca requirement open --idea <idea> [--group <group>] [--language <language>] [--limit <limit>] [--agent <agent>]`

open a requirement from an idea; the group id is generated unless --group names one

- What it does: sends control verb `requirement-open`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `--idea <idea>` (required): what to build
- `--group <group>`: the new group's id
- `--language <language>`: en|zh: the requirement's content language
- `--limit <limit>`: the requirement's budget as JSON {tokens,activeMs,attempts,sessions} — human-only: needs a person token
- `--agent <agent>`: the installation that runs this requirement's agent calls (orca agent list); default: your agent preferences, else the one installed agent when exactly one is

```
orca requirement open --idea "add a dark mode"
orca requirement open --idea "add a dark mode" --agent claude-main
```

## `orca requirement answer <group> [--answer <answer>] [--glossary <glossary>] [--adr <adr>] [--finish]`

answer the current round: --answer <qid> takes the recommendation, --answer <qid>=<text> answers in words; a question not named takes its recommendation and a glossary entry or ADR not named is accepted, as the Web's defaults

- What it does: sends control verb `requirement-answer`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `--answer <answer>` (repeatable): <questionId> or <questionId>=<text>
- `--glossary <glossary>` (repeatable): <id>=accept|reject
- `--adr <adr>` (repeatable): <id>=accept|reject
- `--finish`: close clarification with these answers: no next round is drafted, and the split is drafted from this round (no requirement consensus follows; the answer names the next command, under --json as `next`)

## `orca requirement consensus <group> [--unanswered]`

close clarification at the current round; a round still awaiting answers is refused unless --unanswered

- What it does: sends control verb `requirement-consensus`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `--unanswered`: agree with a round still awaiting answers: its questions stay open and its glossary entries and ADRs are dropped

## `orca requirement continue <group>`

grant exactly one more clarification round after the cap

- What it does: sends control verb `requirement-clarify-more`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix

## `orca requirement revise <group> --round <round> --file <file>`

revise an answered clarification round (a new round; at most one clarify call)

- What it does: sends control verb `requirement-revise`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `--round <round>` (required): the round number to revise
- `--file <file>` (required): the answers JSON {answers, glossaryDecisions, adrDecisions, reason?, exclude?}

## `orca requirement feedback <group> --text <text>`

ask for a new draft of the split

- What it does: sends control verb `requirement-draft-feedback`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `--text <text>` (required): what to change

## `orca requirement resplit <group> --text <text> [--group <group>]`

split an accepted requirement again as a new group (before confirm): the clarification is copied, the new split gets the feedback, this group is archived

- What it does: sends control verb `requirement-resplit`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `--text <text>` (required): what was wrong with the accepted split
- `--group <group>`: the new group's id (default: generated)

```
orca requirement resplit g-1 --text "the two modules do not import each other; run them in parallel"
```

## `orca requirement accept <group> [--despite-conflicts]`

accept the current draft: the group becomes a draft task group; a draft reporting requirement conflicts is refused unless --despite-conflicts

- What it does: sends control verb `requirement-draft-accept`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `--despite-conflicts`: accept a draft whose split reports it does not meet the requirement as written

## `orca requirement apply-parallel <group> [--pair <pair>] [--all]`

drop the dependsOn edges of the parallel-candidate pairs a person names (--pair, repeatable) or of all of them (--all); the result is the next draft

- What it does: sends control verb `requirement-draft-edit`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `--pair <pair>` (repeatable): <before>:<after> of a candidate requirement show lists (repeatable); naming none drops nothing
- `--all`: drop every listed candidate's edge (the old one-shot behaviour)

```
orca requirement show g1   # lists the candidates, each as before ∥ after
orca requirement apply-parallel g1 --pair T3:T4a
orca requirement apply-parallel g1 --all
```

## `orca requirement add-implied-path <group> --task <task> --path <path>`

add a path the current draft lists as implied to that task's target paths; the result is the next draft

- What it does: sends control verb `requirement-draft-edit`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `--task <task>` (required): the task whose success condition names the path
- `--path <path>` (required): the path, as requirement show lists it

```
orca requirement add-implied-path g1 --task cli --path README.md
```

## `orca requirement narrow-path <group> --task <task> --path <path> --to <to>`

replace one of a task's target paths in the current draft with paths inside it; the result is the next draft

- What it does: sends control verb `requirement-draft-edit`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `--task <task>` (required): the task whose target path is narrowed
- `--path <path>` (required): the target path as the draft lists it (for example src/**)
- `--to <to>` (required) (repeatable): a path inside it the task writes (repeatable)

```
orca requirement show g1   # lists 'run one after the other only because their target paths overlap'
orca requirement narrow-path g1 --task velocity --path 'src/**' --to src/report/velocity.js
```

## `orca requirement drop-path <group> --task <task> --path <path>`

remove one of a task's target paths in the current draft (never its last); the result is the next draft

- What it does: sends control verb `requirement-draft-edit`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `--task <task>` (required): the task whose target path is removed
- `--path <path>` (required): the target path as the draft lists it

```
orca requirement show g1   # health-model lists src/health/report.js, which only health-report writes
orca requirement drop-path g1 --task health-model --path src/health/report.js
```

## `orca requirement classify <group> --scope <scope> --clarity <clarity>`

set the requirement's class (it sets the clarification caps)

- What it does: sends control verb `requirement-classify`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `--scope <scope>` (required): small|medium|large
- `--clarity <clarity>` (required): the clarity class

## `orca requirement set-agent <group> [--agent <agent>] [--model <model>]`

re-select the requirement's agent; a round or draft blocked on the old one is drafted again

- What it does: sends control verb `requirement-set-agent`.
- Who may: open over the socket (a flag marked human-only still needs a person token).
- `<group>`: a group id or a unique prefix
- `--agent <agent>`: the installation (orca agent list); default: as your agent preferences choose
- `--model <model>`: the model, as the installation's catalog lists it (orca agent models <installation>)

```
orca requirement set-agent g-1 --model tokenswitch/mode-x
orca requirement set-agent g-1 --agent codex-main --model gpt-5
```
